scope: Offline, simulation-only study; not protocol conformance, railway safety or operational equipment evaluation

protection_model.selected: Simplified preplanned, deterministic, ring-segment-constrained rerouting for each single physical-link fault
protection_model.conformance_claim: NOT RFC 8227 MSRP compliant; explicitly a scenario-based surrogate
protection_model.normal_state: Ordered, ring-valid route segments joined only at legal gateway nodes; no mid-route cycles
protection_model.failure_state: For each failed physical link, use a precomputed permissible alternative ordered ring arc for every affected segment, with the original inter-ring gateway sequence kept fixed in v1; unaffected segments remain unchanged. A plan failing any scenario is rejected.
forbidden: On-demand unconstrained shortest-path search after a fault
Calling two global disjoint paths a full MSRP model
protection_model.optional_future_extension: Implement RFC 8227 ring tunnels, switching mechanism and interconnection node group explicitly, with separate conformance tests

capacity_model.physical_link: Each undirected NetworkX edge corresponds to one physical link ID; its two directed arc budgets are separate; shared ring membership does not duplicate capacity
capacity_model.budget_semantics: Scenario-based robust capacity, max-of-single-fault outcomes. Separate no-fault and every one-physical-link-failure demand evaluated; no packet queue, CIR/CBS policing, or actual protection reservation messages modeled.
capacity_model.admission_rule: For every surviving directed arc a and each permitted scenario f including none: sum admitted service directional reserved rates traversing a in f <= C_usable[a]; failed physical link cannot carry either direction. Reject candidate atomically on any violation.
capacity_model.rounding_policy: All rates integer Mb/s; C_usable rounded down to integer Mb/s; no floating-point boundary tolerance for capacity ledger

failure_model.included: Normal state + exhaustive single physical-link failures; each failure removes BOTH directions of that physical link
failure_model.link_fault_set: Unique physical_link_id values, not ring membership references

traffic.meaning: Each accepted service requests b Mbps from source to destination and b Mbps reverse; verify both directional path plans and fault states. A future asymmetric option must be separately defined.
traffic.priority: Weights used for evaluation/optional reward; not permission to override hard feasibility
traffic.service_lifetime: Admitted services persist until episode end; no release, preemption or modifications in baseline study
traffic.request_sequence: Sequential online arrivals; same train/validation/test split and candidates across all algorithms
traffic.acceptance: Reject if mandatory protected feasibility cannot be guaranteed; optimizer may choose among only feasible options
traffic.reverse_route_rule: For surrogate v1, the reverse direction uses the exact reverse of the normal or fault-state forward physical-node path and reserves the same b Mbps on reverse directed arcs.

model_validation.first_request: Example 200 Mb/s operational service; select actual valid endpoints from generated topology, not assumed numeric addresses
required_tests: normal and each fault path is valid and policy-allowed
both directions of a failed physical link unusable
shared physical edge counted once even with multiple ring memberships
normal case fits but at least one fault case exceeds capacity -> reject
atomic rejection leaves all prior reservations unchanged
all algorithms use identical independent feasibility validator
explicitly detect cases with graph connectivity but no policy-valid protected plan

review.notes: Decide before interpreting Phase 3 results; can begin prototypes pending approval but report decision status clearly.
